title: 28-20 Us, Because I'm a Full-Fledged Masochist
seoTitle: Commanders at Giants Prediction: Brad Rogers' Crew, 'Ask Blough' and a 28-20 Call
summary: Commanders at Giants on Thursday night: Brad Rogers' crew by the numbers, the best lines from this week's press conferences, the group chat's trade deadline, and a 28-20 pick with an actual winner attached.
wireTaps: 28-20 Commanders. Yes, I picked a winner. Yes, I'm worried about it.
paragraphs: On Saturday I said 20-17 and refused to name a winner. The Rams took that as an invitation and won 20-13. So the only part of my prediction that held up was the part where I didn't commit to anything. This week I'm doing the bravest thing a man with a 2-5-1 team can do. I'm picking us. Out loud. On a Thursday.
Links up top, like always: [who's reffing tonight](whos-reffing.html), and [Call Your Shot](leaderboard.html), where you can pick the score before kickoff. Picks lock at 8:15.
## Ref Watch: Brad Rogers, Thursday Specialist

Tonight's referee is Brad Rogers. I checked twice, because I have been burned before. His crews throw 12.5 flags a game, 12th of the 17 refs with enough games to rank and almost a full flag under the 13.4 league average. Boring. Beautiful. Exactly what I asked John Hussey for last week.

Here's the fun part. Brad Rogers has had us twice, and both were Thursdays: Week 2 last year at Green Bay, and Christmas against Dallas. We lost both, 27-18 and 30-23. And in fairness to Brad, neither one was on him. In Green Bay we gained 11 yards in the first quarter. On Christmas we were down 21-3 before anybody had finished their ham. He flagged the Packers 10 times that night and us 5. The man has done nothing wrong. He just keeps showing up on Thursdays, and we keep being bad at Thursdays.

The catch, because there's always a catch: his crews flag the road team a touch more, 6.5 a game to 6.0. We're the road team. I've decided that's a rounding error. Every game he's worked and every ref ranked is on the [Ref Watch page](whos-reffing.html).
## What They Said This Week
I've had the team's press conferences broken down all week, and I'm embarrassed to say I didn't read a single one until last night. They're good. Here's what stuck.

Ask Blough. Somebody asked Jayden why the tight ends not named Chig Okonkwo never catch the ball. He laughed and said you'll have to ask Blough. The next day somebody asked Dan Quinn the same thing, and Quinn said yes, he's surprised too, and he'd like more from them. So the official team position on the tight ends is that everyone is confused, including the people in charge of the tight ends.

Not a must-win, though. On Monday Quinn said, "man, we need this win this week." On Tuesday he still wouldn't call it a must-win. Coach, those are the same sentence. I respect the footwork. Same press conference, a reporter said he'd been around "some," and Quinn thanked him for not saying a really long time, like other people do. That's the most relatable thing a head coach has ever said.
Three centers. Nick Allegretti moves back to center tonight, which makes three centers this season for Jayden. He says the shuffling doesn't throw him off. He's a better man than me.

The 60 percent problem. The Giants blitzed Jayden about 60 percent of the time in October. His fix is "having answers," checks at the line and protections built into the plays. My fix is closing my eyes, so I'm glad he's the quarterback.
Zero incompletions. Quinn said the offense didn't throw one incompletion in Wednesday's practice. In practice. Against our own defense. I'm choosing to believe this is predictive.

Quinn showed the team the endings. He sat everybody down and showed them how the recent Giants games ended, going back to 2024, and five of them came down to the final minutes. I like to think the 27-27 one got shown twice, in slow motion, with the clock circled in red.

And one from last week that aged like milk. Daronte Jones said the plan for Puka Nacua was "premium awareness," meaning every guy in coverage had to know where Puka was before the snap. Puka caught 14 balls. In fairness, we were all very aware of him.

Injury notes: Treylon Burks sat out Wednesday on purpose to be ready tonight, and Lucas Patrick and Colson Yankoff are out. Every breakdown is on the site under the videos, flagged "Breakdown," if you want the full versions.
## The Group Chat Ran the Trade Deadline

I didn't get pregame takes out of the boys this week, because they were busy running the franchise. Jason set the tone Monday morning. "I don't really get mad anymore when I just know other teams' players are better. Like the Rams are a better team. But I just still get so frustrated with general football incompetence." Jason, that's the whole fan experience in three sentences. Put it on the shirt next to Quinn's.

Then Chris went full general manager. "It's time to sell anyone with value outside JD5. We gotta go full Indy." Eighteen seconds later: "except we don't really have anyone other teams want." A complete rebuild, start to finish. Adam Peters needed the whole trade deadline to do nothing. Chris did it in eighteen seconds.

Jason's one real trade idea was sending Marcus Mariota to Minnesota. Chris agreed and set the price at a 4th. The next day Minnesota went and got Kirk Cousins instead, our old quarterback, for a 3rd. Jason took the news like a gentleman: "I hope they win it all. I love Kirk Cousins." Chris then found a stat where Mariota is fifth in the NFL in QB rating. You just have to set the minimum at 50 attempts. Every backup is an MVP if you squint.

Chris also pointed out that as bad as we've been, we still only have the 7th pick. We can't even suck good. I wrote a [whole post](blog-original-we-cant-even-suck-good.html) about this. His long-term plan is to just suck for a while and build it right, because he's "sick of trying to constantly slap bandaids on a gaping wound." His short-term plan, as far as I can tell, is learning to fish. On Wednesday: "I'm trying to be an outdoors guy when at the lake. But I can't tie a simple knot for my fishing pole." I asked if he'd thrown his pole into the lake again. He did not answer, which I'm counting as a yes.

One more Chris note. He wants me to turn on comments on this website, mostly because he wants to see if people comment on his bathroom. Chris, we have [Roll Call](roll-call.html). People can say whatever they want about your bathroom there. Readers, it's open.
## My Number: 28-20
The last time I picked a winner against the Giants, I said 24-20: "We keep it close, per usual, and then we pull away." It ended 27-27. We did both. Just in the wrong order.

Vegas has the Giants by two and a half, with the total at 40.5. They're 5-2-1 and leading the division. We're 2-5-1, and as I told the group chat Monday, we're on life support. But the NFC East still blows. Philly has lost seven straight, Dallas is 4-5, and a win tonight puts us two games back with half a season to go. The oxygen tank isn't empty yet.

So here it is, in writing: Commanders 28, Giants 20. Just enough to keep us interested in the season, and because I'm a full-fledged masochist. That's 48 points in a game Vegas thinks will have 40. I'm taking the over on our offense and the over on my own suffering.

Here's the other part of the masochism. I'm still somehow first on the [leaderboard](leaderboard.html) with a 1-2 record, mostly because I didn't pick a winner last week, and you can't lose a pick you never made. Picking one tonight means I can finally lose first place. Please don't take it from me. Actually, do. [Call your shot](leaderboard.html) and come get it.
Thursday, 8:15, Prime Video, at MetLife. A night game on a work night. If this one goes to overtime again, Friday me is going to have some words for Thursday me.

Quinn says he expects another close one, and five straight endings say he's right. So I have one request, and it's the same one I had in October. If it comes down to the last minute, and it will, clock it. Hail.
